title: Sign in and registration
summary: Enter an existing workspace or start a new one.
implemented: Required-field validation, password visibility, autofill and return routing use the same access flow.
deferred: Credentials and sessions are simulated; no identity provider.

examples.label: Sign in
examples.instruction: Submit the form or follow Create an account.

examples.label: Register
examples.instruction: Choose account details, then name the workspace.

title: Social / OAuth Provider Buttons
summary: Choose a provider, continue with a sample identity and return to the intended workflow.
implemented: Google and GitHub local demos share the password and email-link handoff: enabled MFA for sign-in, onboarding and selected-plan retention for registration. Cancellation, unavailable attempts, retry and single-use callbacks have recovery paths.
deferred: Local simulation only. No OAuth exchange, provider connection, credentials, account linking or production authorization.

examples.label: Provider sign-in
examples.instruction: Choose Google or GitHub, then Continue with the sample account. Cancel returns to the available methods. Enabled two-step verification is retained.

examples.label: Register with a plan
examples.instruction: Choose a provider and continue into workspace setup. The selected Business yearly plan is carried through onboarding.

examples.label: Provider unavailable
examples.instruction: Continue to the unavailable result, then try again or use another sign-in method.

title: Passwordless Magic Link Flow
summary: Let people sign in through a single-use email link.
implemented: Email request, receipt, replacement link and callback return to the intended local page. Missing, replaced, used and reload-lost links offer recovery; sign-in links remain separate from password resets.
deferred: Local simulation only: no email delivery or authentication provider, timed expiry, rate limiting or cross-device sign-in.

examples.label: Request a sign-in link
examples.instruction: Enter a sample email, request a link and follow Open demo sign-in link. Request another link to replace the first.

title: 2FA / TOTP 6-Digit Input
summary: Complete a second-factor challenge with a clear recovery path.
implemented: Six-digit entry, paste, explicit verification and single-use recovery codes. Security settings supports setup, replacement and disabling; password, email-link and provider demos use the enabled second step and retain the intended destination.
deferred: Local simulation with a disclosed fixed code. No TOTP secret, QR enrollment, real identity provider, authorization, lockout or device trust.

examples.label: Set up and try verification
examples.instruction: Enable two-step verification with demo code 123456, save the recovery codes, then use Try sign-in. Every sign-in method continues to verification.

title: Multi-Step Onboarding Stepper
summary: Show progress through a multi-step workspace setup.
implemented: Named Workspace, Team and Ready steps retain drafts on Back, allow invitations to be skipped and focus the new heading.
deferred: Progress is local to the current demo session; no server-backed resume.

examples.label: Set up a workspace
examples.instruction: Register, name the workspace, then invite colleagues or skip to the summary.

title: Workspace setup
summary: Give a new workspace its identity before starting work.
implemented: Workspace details and optional invitation rows remain drafts until setup finishes. Completion creates the workspace and pending invitations together, then offers Projects and Team settings.
deferred: Slug availability, setup avatar, real invitation delivery and a guided tour remain planned.

examples.label: Create a workspace
examples.instruction: Register, enter a workspace name, and try invitation roles, Back navigation or Skip for now.

title: Password recovery
summary: Recover access without losing the intended destination.
implemented: Local request, receipt, single-use reset link and sign-in return.
deferred: Email delivery and stored passwords are not implemented.

examples.label: Request a reset
examples.instruction: Submit an email, then use the local link on the receipt page.

examples.label: Unavailable link
examples.instruction: Request a fresh link from the recovery state.

title: Inactivity / Session Expiry Modal
summary: Recover from an expired session without losing current work.
implemented: A session-expiry specimen resumes the fixture account through a dialog while preserving the current draft.
deferred: No inactivity timer, production session expiry or credential exchange is implemented.

examples.label: Resume a session
examples.instruction: Try the recovery action, then Reset to restore the starting fixture.

title: Workspace metrics
summary: Summarize the current state of project work.
implemented: Four totals shown as one metric strip with hairline dividers, derived from the same projects used by the table and board.
deferred: Historical comparisons and asynchronous loading remain planned.

examples.label: Workspace snapshot
examples.instruction: Compare active projects, tasks remaining, near-term due dates and completions.

title: Completion time series
summary: See how completed work changes over time.
implemented: Daily bars for the chosen period or custom range, with Completed and Added totals in the heading that choose the series (shadcn's interactive bar chart), the snapshot day at full strength, and Show data with both columns in the chart's place. Completions come from Activity and additions from task creation dates, over about 90 days of history.
deferred: None for the daily series; Analytics' Delivery section carries the multi-series variants (DVIZ-06, DVIZ-07, DVIZ-09).

examples.label: Last 30 days
examples.instruction: Choose Added in the heading, change the period, or choose Show data.

examples.label: Last 7 days
examples.instruction: The chart and total use the same seven-day scope.

title: Project completion bars
summary: Compare completed work across projects.
implemented: Single-series horizontal bars with labels and a linked data alternative.
deferred: Grouped/stacked bars and legend filtering remain planned.

examples.label: Project breakdown
examples.instruction: Use the project breakdown or switch to its data view.

title: Contributor breakdown
summary: Understand the share of work completed by each contributor.
implemented: Donut chart, stable member colors, visible values and a data table.
deferred: No hover-only data or historical comparison is supplied.

examples.label: Contributor breakdown
examples.instruction: Inspect the contributor breakdown and its table alternative.

title: Reporting scope
summary: Keep several views aligned to one reporting period.
implemented: Overview and Analytics share a 7/14/30/90-day period or a custom range (up to 92 days) in the URL, plus a project filter on Analytics. The shown dates open the range calendar; the snapshot day is emphasised only when the range includes it. Analytics' Compare with previous period (compare=true) adds the period of the same length just before to Delivery's headings and a dashed line, and says when there is no history to compare with.
deferred: Comparison against a chosen period (rather than the one just before) is not offered.

examples.label: Reporting filters
examples.instruction: Choose Custom range, pick two days, then share the URL; charts and totals update together.

examples.label: Overview period
examples.instruction: Select the dates above the chart.

title: Inline and dialog project editing

deferred: Browser connectivity detection, durable offline storage and network retries are not implemented.

examples.label: Offline editing
examples.instruction: Try the recovery action, then Reset to restore the starting fixture.

examples.instruction: Try the recovery action, then Reset to restore the starting fixture.

examples.label: Cards

examples.label: Table
examples.instruction: Compare fields across rows.

examples.label: Board
examples.instruction: Compare work by status.

title: Advanced Query Builder
summary: Build advanced combinations of conditions when simple facets are insufficient.
implemented: On-demand Match all/any conditions for name, status, owner, due date and progress. Apply commits the draft; Cancel discards it. Validated URL filters share result membership, counts and selection across Table, Cards and Board.
deferred: Nested condition groups, saved queries and server-side querying remain separate work.

examples.label: Advanced project filters
examples.instruction: Open Advanced, add conditions and apply them. Switch views or visit a project; the applied filters remain in the URL.

title: Tooltips and dotted text hints
summary: Reveal supplementary explanations without clutter or layout shift.
implemented: Shared dotted-underlined TextHint uses a hoverable, tappable Popover. Icon tooltips supplement accessible button names. Includes a live Overview term and reference specimen.
deferred: Important instructions stay visible. Physical touch-device and screen-reader verification remain separate.

examples.label: Text hints and icon tooltips
examples.instruction: Hover or activate Active projects; dismiss with Escape or outside interaction. Try the labelled bookmark action.

examples.label: Due date definition
examples.instruction: Hover or activate the dotted-underlined Due in 7 days label.

title: Page actions in the top bar
originalName: Page actions in the top bar
summary: Put a page's primary action and short context in the top bar instead of a heading row.
implemented: PageActions/PageAction portal a page's action and metadata into the shell's top bar; the action shows only its icon on phones and keeps its label as the accessible name.
deferred: Overflow menus for several actions remain planned.

examples.label: New project and snapshot date
examples.instruction: Use New project in the top bar; narrow the window to see the icon-only form.

title: Identity colour picker
summary: Choose a record's identity colour from a small named palette, previewed live.
implemented: Six named swatches as a radio group in the project editor; the heading mark updates live and the saved colour drives dots, progress bars and chart series.
deferred: Custom colours are out of scope; colour changes are not written to activity.

examples.label: Project colour
examples.instruction: Pick a swatch, watch the heading mark change, then save and open the project.

title: Palette generator
summary: Derive a readable brand palette for light and dark from one colour.
implemented: Seed colour and optional neutral tint generate brand tokens for both modes; lightness moves until links, fills and soft fills reach 4.5:1, and adjustments are named.
deferred: Status and categorical hues are not generated.

examples.label: Generate tab
examples.instruction: Open Customize, choose Generate and try a light seed such as #facc15.

title: Theme export to shadcn
summary: Export a theme as a registry item that installs into another project.
implemented: Import / export offers a registry:theme item that installs its own override file after the kit tokens with `npx shadcn add`.
deferred: Installing a theme as an extra accent remains planned.

examples.label: shadcn export
examples.instruction: Open Import / export and choose the shadcn tab.

title: Switch
summary: Toggle a setting on or off with an immediate effect.
implemented: Kit Switch on Base UI in two sizes; notification preferences use it for each channel.
deferred: No workspace-level feature toggles yet.

examples.label: Notifications
examples.instruction: Turn a channel on or off, then save.

title: Slider
summary: Pick a value or range along a track with keyboard steps.
deferred: Planned. Demo target: seat count in billing plan selection.

title: Progress
summary: Show completion as a labelled bar driven by tokens.
implemented: Kit Progress on Base UI with label and value parts; project bars set --progress-color to the project's hue.
deferred: No indeterminate state.

examples.label: Project progress
examples.instruction: Compare the bar with the task count.

examples.label: Progress reference
examples.instruction: Complete a task.

title: Calendar and date picker
summary: Choose a date from a calendar that follows density and theme.
implemented: Kit Calendar (react-day-picker) and DatePicker with ISO values, Monday weeks, keyboard navigation and a name that includes the chosen date. Project due dates use it in the editor and the Details dialog.
deferred: No typed date entry or time of day.

examples.label: Due date
examples.instruction: Open Due date and choose a day.

examples.label: Details dialog
examples.instruction: Choose Edit beside Details, then open Due date.

title: Date-range picker
summary: Choose a start and end date with presets.
implemented: Kit DateRangePicker: two months, a fresh range on each opening, a latest date and a maximum span, applied on the second click.
deferred: No preset list inside the popover; hosts pair it with their own presets.

examples.label: Reporting dates
examples.instruction: Select the dates above the chart and choose two days.

title: Hover card
summary: Preview a person or record on hover or focus without navigating.
implemented: Kit HoverCard on Base UI Preview Card. Owner names in the Projects table and people in Activity are links that filter the view to that person; hovering or focusing one previews their role, email, owned projects and open tasks from the shared demo state.
deferred: No hover cards on avatars alone, which are not links.

examples.label: Project owners
examples.instruction: Hover or tab to an owner's name, then follow it.

examples.label: Activity people
examples.instruction: Hover a person's name.

examples.label: Hover card reference
examples.instruction: Hover the owner.

title: Context menu
summary: Offer row or card actions on right-click and the keyboard menu key.
implemented: Kit ContextMenu sharing the dropdown menu's items. Board cards offer the same actions as their menu button (details, reorder, move to a status with Undo); Projects table rows offer View details, Open project and Select. The inspector returns focus to the item's inspect button.
deferred: No submenus or multi-item context actions.

examples.label: Board cards
examples.instruction: Right-click or long-press a card.

examples.label: Table rows
examples.instruction: Right-click a row and choose Select.

examples.label: Context menu reference
examples.instruction: Right-click the file.

title: Keyboard key
summary: Show a key or shortcut consistently.
implemented: Kit Kbd and KbdGroup in the shortcut list and as the search hint, with the platform's modifier key.
deferred: No shortcut hints inside menus.

examples.label: Search hint
examples.instruction: Find Ctrl K (⌘ K on a Mac) beside Find a project.

examples.label: Shortcuts
examples.instruction: Press ? to open the shortcut list.

title: Spinner
summary: Signal a short wait inside a control without layout shift.
implemented: Kit Spinner with a status role and label, used inside loading buttons.
deferred: No page-level loading overlay.

examples.label: Loading button
examples.instruction: Select Publish update.

title: Scroll area
summary: Scroll a bounded region with themed, unobtrusive scrollbars.
implemented: Kit ScrollArea on Base UI: native scrolling with a thin overlay scrollbar. The Inbox message list uses it (keeping scroll restoration on the viewport), and Overview's Recent activity uses its overflow variables to fade only the edges with more history, replacing hand-written scroll measuring.
deferred: No horizontal scroll areas yet; wide tables keep native scrolling.

examples.label: Inbox list
examples.instruction: Make the window short and scroll the messages.

examples.label: Recent activity
examples.instruction: Scroll the activity beside the chart.

examples.label: Scroll area reference
examples.instruction: Scroll the release history.

title: Carousel
summary: Browse a row of items with buttons, swipe and keys.
implemented: Kit Carousel on native scroll snapping: named carousel and slides, Previous/Next by one visible page that disable at the ends, reduced-motion jumps, no auto-advance and no dependency. Home's customer stories use it.
deferred: No autoplay, pagination dots or looping.

examples.label: Customer stories
examples.instruction: Use Next beside Teams that plan in Tandem.

examples.label: Carousel reference
examples.instruction: Scroll or use the buttons.

title: Drawer
summary: Bottom sheet for phone-sized actions and filters.
implemented: Kit Drawer on Base UI, and a kit FacetDrawer for data tables. On phones, Projects replaces its Status and Owner buttons with one Filters drawer of checkbox lists with counts, Clear filters and Show N projects; Activity's phone filters open in a drawer with Show N events.
deferred: No snap points or nested drawers in the demo.

examples.label: Projects filters
examples.instruction: At phone width, open Filters.

examples.label: Activity filters
examples.instruction: At phone width, open Filters.

examples.label: Drawer reference
examples.instruction: Open Sort and choose an order.

title: Project task list
summary: Break a project into tasks whose completion drives its progress.
implemented: Project tasks behind an Open/Completed switch in the page's Tasks tab: complete, reopen, assign, reorder and delete (with Undo). A task ticked or unticked stays in the list until the view changes. Titles open a rich-text description that edits in place; Add task is a dialog with title, assignee and description. Each project's counts derive from its tasks; completing a task records it in Activity and Analytics, and Mark complete completes the remaining tasks. Completed projects show their tasks read-only.
deferred: No task due dates, subtasks or drag reordering; menu commands move tasks.

examples.label: Project tasks
examples.instruction: Tick two tasks and watch 24 of 32 change; open a task's title and edit its description; add a task.

title: Comments and mentions
summary: Discuss a record in a thread and notify people with @mentions.
implemented: Project comments in the page's Comments tab, as a thread with a composer that suggests teammates after @ (arrow keys, Enter or Tab, Escape). Mentions are stored as member tokens and highlighted; posting records a Comment event in Activity. Teammates' comments that mention the current user appear in the inbox and notifications.
deferred: No editing, deleting, reactions or threaded replies; mentioning someone else sends no notification in this single-user demo.

examples.label: Brand refresh comments
examples.instruction: Type @ in Add a comment, choose a teammate and post.

examples.label: Mentions in the inbox
examples.instruction: Open a Mentioned you in a comment message.

title: File attachments
summary: Attach files by drag and drop with progress, preview and removal.
implemented: Project files beside progress: thumbnails, a preview dialog with download, and remove with Undo. Drop or choose files; each upload shows labelled progress, files over 10 MB are refused before starting, and scenario=upload-failure interrupts the first upload with Retry.
deferred: Upload progress is simulated (no network); uploaded files live in memory and are gone after a reload.

examples.label: Brand refresh files
examples.instruction: Choose a file to upload, then open Primary palette.

examples.label: Upload failure
examples.instruction: Upload a file; the first attempt fails, then Retry.

title: Timeline and calendar view
summary: See projects across time by due date.
implemented: view=timeline shows every matching project as a bar from its first activity to its due date, filled to the share of tasks done, with weekly gridlines, a snapshot-date line and a pinned name column. A Month layout places due dates on a Monday-first calendar and becomes a list of due days on phones.
deferred: No dragging bars to reschedule and no start-date field.

examples.label: Timeline
examples.instruction: Compare bars with the snapshot line, then choose Month.

title: CSV import with column mapping
summary: Bring records in from a spreadsheet by mapping columns and reviewing problems.
implemented: Import on Projects opens a four-step page: upload (or the sample file), map columns with guessed matches and examples, review every row with its line and problems (missing name, bad date, unknown owner, duplicate), then import the ready rows through the editor's own save. Skipped rows say why.
deferred: No inline fixing of rows, status column or undo of an import.

examples.label: Import projects
examples.instruction: Choose Use the sample file, review the rows and import.

title: Saved views
summary: Save and reopen a named combination of filters, sort and view.
implemented: A Views menu beside the view switch lists three team views and your own. The button names the view that matches the current filters, sort and layout; Save current view asks for a unique name, Copy link copies the URL that reproduces it, and your own views can be deleted.
deferred: Saved views last for the session; no sharing to teammates, pinning or per-view columns.

examples.label: Saved views
examples.instruction: Open Views, choose My open work, then save a view of your own.

title: Getting-started checklist
summary: Guide a new workspace through its first useful steps.
implemented: After a workspace is created through onboarding, Overview opens with a Get started list: create a project, add tasks, invite the team, start a conversation. Each step ticks itself from the workspace records, shows its progress and links to where it happens; Hide removes it for the session.
deferred: No per-step dismissal or persistence across reloads.

examples.label: Get started
examples.instruction: Create an account and a workspace, skip invitations, then open Overview.

title: Undo after destructive actions
summary: Let people reverse a removal for a short time instead of confirming up front.
implemented: Status and owner changes apply at once and can be reversed: a toast after Mark complete or a board move, and an inline Undo beside the bulk outcome. Undo restores earlier values and removes the change's activity, keeping later edits.
deferred: Tag and link removal keep their current immediate behaviour; no undo history beyond the latest change.

examples.label: Bulk undo
examples.instruction: Select two projects, mark them complete, then select Undo.

examples.label: Board move
examples.instruction: Move a card from its Actions menu, then Undo in the toast.

title: Search results page
summary: Show grouped results across projects, people, messages and help.
implemented: Typing in Ctrl/⌘ K search offers Search everything first, so Enter opens /app/demo/search: grouped projects, tasks, comments, messages, people and help guides with counts, type filters, highlighted matches and links to each record (comments open at the comment). Query and type live in the URL; a project opened from it names Search in its breadcrumb, which returns to the results.
deferred: No ranking beyond title-first, fuzzy matching or recent searches.

examples.label: Search results
examples.instruction: Press Ctrl or ⌘ K, type a word and press Enter.

title: Integrations directory
summary: Browse integrations by category with search and detail pages.
implemented: /integrations lists nine fictional integrations with a search and category toggles that combine, a live count, Beta and Coming soon badges, and an empty state. Filters wrap on narrow screens.
deferred: No per-integration detail pages or connect flow.

examples.label: Integrations
examples.instruction: Choose Developer, then search webhook.

title: Customer story
summary: Tell one team's story with results, quotes and product shots.
implemented: /customers lists four fictional sample stories; /customers/:slug tells one: company and size, outcome headline, three figures in the story's hue, the team's quote, problem/change/result sections, a way into the demo and the other stories. Unknown slugs explain themselves.
deferred: No filtering by industry or real customer content.

examples.label: Customers
examples.instruction: Open a story.

examples.label: A story
examples.instruction: Read the figures and quote.

title: About and careers
summary: Present the company, values and open roles.
implemented: /about tells the sample team's story, three numbered values and four open roles (#careers), each linking to Contact. The footer's Careers link lands on the roles.
deferred: No role detail pages or application form.

examples.label: About
examples.instruction: Scroll to Open roles.

examples.label: Careers
examples.instruction: Follow Ask about this role.

title: Public roadmap
summary: Show planned, in-progress and shipped work, with voting.
implemented: /roadmap groups sample ideas as Now, Next, Later and Shipped. Planned ideas have a pressed-state vote toggle kept in session memory across navigation; shipped ones link to the changelog.
deferred: No idea submission, comments or sorting.

examples.label: Roadmap
examples.instruction: Vote for Guest access, visit Status, come back.

title: Status page
summary: Report service health, incidents and uptime history.
implemented: /status shows the overall state, five components with 90 daily bars, uptime and state, and three past incidents with timed updates. It says the demo has no live service.
deferred: No subscriptions, live data or scheduled maintenance.

examples.label: Status
examples.instruction: Compare the API and Notifications rows with the incidents.

title: Stats band
summary: Highlight a few numbers in the brand voice.
implemented: A Home band in the display face: 218 tasks tracked, 68 completed in two weeks, 6 projects, 4 people, computed from the same fixtures the demo opens with, with a link into it.
deferred: No animated counting or live figures.

examples.label: Stats band
examples.instruction: Scroll past the features.

title: How it works
summary: Explain the product in three or four numbered steps.
implemented: Product's How it works: four numbered steps (import, tasks, comments and files, timeline and saved views), each linking to that place in the sample workspace.
deferred: No illustrations or video per step.

examples.label: How it works
examples.instruction: Scroll below the product tabs and follow a step.

title: Announcement bar
summary: Promote one timely update above the header, dismissibly.
implemented: A slim bar above the public header (kit AnnouncementBar) names the latest release and links to its notes. Dismissing it is remembered per release in local storage, like other display preferences; a newer release shows again.
deferred: One announcement at a time; no scheduling.

examples.label: Announcement
examples.instruction: Read the bar at the top, then dismiss it.

title: Chat conversation
summary: Hold a conversation with an assistant: a transcript that follows replies, with a clear empty state and progress.
implemented: The Assistant page streams scripted replies through the AI SDK's useChat and a local transport. Each question is anchored at the top while the reply grows below it; a jump button returns to the latest reply. The transcript is not announced token by token: a status region says the assistant is replying and then reads the finished reply. Thinking… shimmers until the first words arrive; Stop keeps the partial reply and marks it; a failed reply shows Try again where it failed (?scenario=assistant-error).
deferred: Conversations last until reload.

examples.label: Assistant
examples.instruction: Ask Which projects are at risk?, then stop a longer reply part-way.

examples.label: Failed reply
examples.instruction: Ask a question, wait for the failure, then choose Try again.

title: Streaming markdown response
summary: Render a model's markdown as it streams, with kit typography, tables, links and code.
implemented: MessageResponse renders markdown with Streamdown, which keeps half-finished syntax readable while it streams. Every element uses kit classes; fenced code becomes the kit Code block; the host passes a link renderer so workspace links route in-app.
deferred: No maths, diagrams or images in replies yet.

examples.label: API answer
examples.instruction: Ask How do I list projects with the API? and watch the code blocks stream.

title: Prompt composer
summary: Write a message to a model: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, and the send button becomes Stop while a reply streams.
implemented: PromptInput is a rounded surface: attachments, text that grows up to a limit, then a row with the + menu, model and context tools and a round send button whose tooltip carries the keys. Enter sends unless an input method is composing; while the model works the button stops the reply and Enter queues the message (AI-13). The button never disables, so focus stays put. Before the first message it sits in the middle of the page under a larger heading, and a view transition moves it to the bottom once the conversation starts.

examples.label: Assistant composer
examples.instruction: Write two lines with Shift+Enter, send, then draft a follow-up while it replies.

title: Suggested prompts
summary: Offer questions the assistant can answer, as one-click prompts.
implemented: The empty conversation offers three starting questions; each reply streams follow-up questions as an AI SDK data part, shown under the latest reply only. Choosing one sends it and returns focus to the composer.

examples.label: Suggestions
examples.instruction: Choose a starting question, then a follow-up under the reply.

title: Message actions
summary: Act on a reply: copy it, or ask for another version.
implemented: Icon actions under each finished reply carry tooltips that match their accessible names. Copy confirms in place and reports failure; Regenerate appears on the latest reply and replaces it.
deferred: No helpful/unhelpful feedback.

examples.label: Reply actions
examples.instruction: Copy a reply, then regenerate the latest one.

title: Code block
summary: Show code with syntax highlighting, a language or file label and a copy button.
implemented: Shiki highlights on demand (the highlighter and each language load on first use) with a CSS-variables theme, so colours come from the --syntax-* tokens and follow light, dark and the accent. Code renders plainly until highlighting is ready, without moving. Long lines scroll inside the block, which is keyboard focusable.
deferred: Eight languages ship; add others in code-block-highlight.ts. No diff or line highlighting yet.

examples.label: Code block reference
examples.instruction: Copy the example and switch to dark mode.

examples.label: In a reply
examples.instruction: Ask How do I list projects with the API?

examples.label: Webhook deliveries
examples.instruction: Open a webhook's deliveries and a delivery's response body.

title: Snippet
summary: Show one command or line of code with a copy button.
implemented: A single scrolling line with an optional prompt prefix that is not copied, and a copy button named after what it copies.

examples.label: API keys
examples.instruction: Copy the request under your keys.

examples.label: Snippet reference
examples.instruction: Copy the install command.

title: Reasoning
summary: Show what a model is thinking while it works, then get it out of the way.
implemented: The at-risk answer streams its reasoning first (a reasoning part). The block opens while it streams, closes when the answer starts and reads Thought for 2 seconds; the person's own open or close sticks.
deferred: Reasoning is not persisted across conversations; its duration is measured on screen.

examples.label: Assistant
examples.instruction: Ask Which projects are at risk? and watch the reasoning open and fold away.

title: Tool call
summary: Show that the assistant called a tool, what it asked for and what came back.
implemented: The at-risk answer calls searchProjects: parameters stream in, the call runs, and the result shows as a readable project list. The row's badge follows the AI SDK tool states. In ?scenario=tool-error the search fails once, the row opens by itself to show why, and the reply says it could not answer; Regenerate succeeds.

examples.label: Tool call
examples.instruction: Ask Which projects are at risk?, then open Search projects.

examples.label: Failed tool call
examples.instruction: Ask Which projects are at risk?, then Regenerate.

title: Sources
summary: List the records a reply drew on so its claims can be checked.
implemented: Replies stream source-url parts after their text; Used 4 sources opens a numbered list of project pages with their status and due date. Links route in-app, and the project page names the Assistant in its breadcrumb to return.
deferred: Document sources (source-document parts) have no demonstration yet.

examples.label: Sources
examples.instruction: Ask Which projects are at risk?, then open Used 4 sources.

title: Inline citation
summary: Attach sources to the sentence they support.
implemented: Reply markdown cites with links to #source:<ids>; the assistant view renders them as numbered pills that link to the first source and preview all of them on hover or focus. Before the sources arrive, the number shows without a preview. Citations are removed from copied text and from the spoken reply.

examples.label: Citations
examples.instruction: Ask Which projects are at risk?, then focus the 2–4 citation.

title: Chain of thought
summary: Report an agent's progress as named steps.
implemented: The weekly summary reports three steps as AI SDK data parts, each sent as in progress and replaced by id when done, with its results as chips. The list shows the current step while it works and folds to Worked through 3 steps.

examples.label: Progress steps
examples.instruction: Ask What changed this week? and watch the steps.

title: Plan
summary: Show what the assistant proposes before it acts.
implemented: Asking for a launch checklist streams a plan as an AI SDK data part updated by id: five tasks arrive one by one, each with its assignee (the project owner takes the first two).
deferred: Plans cannot be edited in place; ask again for a different one.

examples.label: Checklist plan
examples.instruction: Ask Add a launch checklist to Mobile app.

title: Tool approval
summary: Ask before a tool changes anything, then do exactly what was approved.
implemented: The createTasks tool call arrives in the AI SDK's approval-requested state. Add tasks or Don't add answers with addToolApprovalResponse; the chat sends automatically, and the scripted server runs the host's createTasks implementation only when approved. The tasks really appear on the project page (shared demo state, one atomic change); the outcome and an Open project link replace the actions.
deferred: No Undo in the assistant; remove tasks from the project's list. A pending approval in an older reply cannot be answered.

examples.label: Approve
examples.instruction: Ask Add a launch checklist to Brand refresh, choose Add tasks, then Open Brand refresh.

examples.label: Decline
examples.instruction: Ask for a checklist again and choose Don't add.

title: Message queue
summary: Keep messages written while the assistant is busy or waiting, and send them in turn.
implemented: During a reply, Enter queues the message; while a reply waits for an answer or approval, sending queues too. The queue sits above the composer with a remove action per message and says when it will send; each becomes the next prompt once the assistant is ready.
deferred: The queue belongs to the page and is lost on navigation.

examples.label: Queue
examples.instruction: While a checklist waits for approval, send What changed this week?, then choose Add tasks.

title: Clarifying question
summary: Let the assistant ask instead of guessing.
implemented: A checklist request that names no project calls the client-side chooseProject tool. The page renders it as a question listing the open projects; the answer goes back with addToolOutput and the turn continues to the plan automatically.

examples.label: Question
examples.instruction: Choose Add a launch checklist to a project, then pick a project.

title: Conversation history
summary: Keep past conversations to return to, rename or delete.
implemented: Each conversation keeps its own AI SDK Chat in demo state, so switching is instant and a reply can finish in the background. History sits beside the chat on wide screens and opens as a sheet from the top bar below 72rem. Titles come from the first question until renamed in place; Delete offers Undo. New chat reuses an empty conversation instead of piling them up.
deferred: History lasts until reload; no search or grouping by date.

examples.label: History
examples.instruction: Ask two questions in separate chats (New chat), switch between them, then rename and delete one.

title: Reply versions
summary: Keep the replies Regenerate replaces, and move between them.
implemented: Regenerate keeps the reply it replaces as an earlier version of the answer to that question. The latest reply then shows previous and next with its position; choosing a version makes it the reply the conversation continues from.
deferred: Versions are kept for the latest question only; earlier questions keep the version that was shown.

examples.label: Versions
examples.instruction: Ask a question, choose Regenerate, then move back to the first version.

title: Restore to a checkpoint
summary: Go back to before a question, to ask it differently.
implemented: Between turns, Restore (on hover or focus) removes that question and everything after it, puts the question back in the composer and offers Undo. When the removed turns had added tasks, the toast says those stay.

examples.label: Checkpoint
examples.instruction: Ask two questions, then restore to before the second.

title: Attachments and context
summary: Attach files, or a project as context, to a message.
implemented: The composer's + menu adds files from the computer or one of the open projects; files can also be dropped or pasted. Chips show above the text and above the sent message. Files travel as AI SDK file parts (data URLs) and projects as data parts. An attached project counts as named in the question (a checklist goes into it); the scripted assistant says honestly that it cannot read files.
deferred: Files are not read or stored; there is no upload progress because nothing uploads.

examples.label: Attach a project
examples.instruction: Add Mobile app from the + menu, then ask Add a launch checklist.

title: Model choice
summary: Choose how the assistant answers.
implemented: Fast, Balanced and Thorough are sent with each request. Fast answers quicker without visible reasoning; Thorough takes longer over each step. The choice lasts for the session, across chats.

examples.label: Models
examples.instruction: Switch to Fast and ask Which projects are at risk?

title: Context usage
summary: Show how much of the model's window the conversation uses, and roughly what it costs.
implemented: Each reply's finish reports token usage as message metadata (as a server would); the composer's ring shows the latest total against the chosen model's window, with the last input and output and the conversation's estimated cost.
deferred: Token counts are estimates from text length; prices are illustrative.

examples.label: Context
examples.instruction: After a reply, open the ring beside the model name.

title: Drafted artifact
summary: Let the assistant draft something the person takes elsewhere.
implemented: Asking for a status update streams a document as an AI SDK data part: the week's activity, next open tasks and a risk line, from live records. Copy and Download keep the markdown; Post to project adds it as a comment (once), and the footer links to the project. Without a named project the assistant asks which one first.
deferred: Drafts cannot be edited before posting; copy, edit and post from the project instead.

examples.label: Status update
examples.instruction: Ask Draft a status update for Mobile app, then Post to project.

title: Assistant settings
summary: Show what the workspace assistant is and control what it may do.
implemented: Settings › Assistant pairs an Agent summary (instructions, tools, output) with a default model and a switch per tool. Changes apply at once; with a tool off, the assistant explains and links back here instead of answering.
deferred: Instructions are fixed in this demo; the scripted replies could not follow edited ones.

examples.label: Settings › Assistant
examples.instruction: Turn off Search projects, then ask Which projects are at risk?

title: Open in chat
summary: Carry a question about a page into a chat.
implemented: Help guides offer Ask about this guide: the Tandem Assistant opens with the question filled in and answers from the guide, citing it; Open in Claude opens a new tab with the question and the guide's address.
deferred: No ChatGPT entry: its mark is no longer available from Simple Icons, and the kit's chatLinks.chatgpt remains for projects that source it.

examples.label: Help guide
examples.instruction: Open Ask about this guide and choose Ask the Tandem Assistant.

title: Terminal
summary: Show command output with its colours, and follow it while it runs.
implemented: ANSI SGR codes (colour, bold, dim, italic, underline) are parsed into spans coloured by theme roles. While streaming, the view keeps the newest line in sight unless the person has scrolled up, and shows a cursor. Copy takes the plain text; the output is keyboard scrollable.
deferred: No input, cursor movement or 256-colour codes; interactive shells need a terminal emulator such as xterm.js.

examples.label: Coding agent
examples.instruction: Choose Replay and watch the first test run print.

examples.label: Terminal reference
examples.instruction: Copy the output.

title: File tree
summary: Browse a folder hierarchy and pick a file, with changes marked.
implemented: A tree with the ARIA tree keyboard pattern and one tab stop. Folders open and close; selecting a file reports its path. Added, modified and deleted files carry A, M or D, also spoken. In the specimen, files are marked once the agent edits them, and selecting one previews it.
deferred: No type-ahead, multi-select, drag and drop or lazy loading of large folders.

examples.label: Coding agent
examples.instruction: Move through Files with the arrow keys and open package.json.

examples.label: File tree reference
examples.instruction: Collapse src with the Left arrow.

title: Commit
summary: Summarise a commit and the files it changed.
implemented: Message, short hash, body, author and date, then each file with lines added and removed, coloured and stated in words.
deferred: No links to a repository host or per-file diffs.

examples.label: Coding agent
examples.instruction: Scroll to the Commit step.

examples.label: Commit reference
examples.instruction: Compare the three files' changes.

title: Test results
summary: Report a test run so failures stand out and can be read in place.
implemented: A summary (failed count or All passed, passed of total, duration), a passed/failed/skipped bar and each suite's tests with status in words, icon and colour. A failing test can show its stack trace underneath.
deferred: No filtering, re-run or history across runs.

examples.label: Coding agent
examples.instruction: Read the failing test, then the passing run after the fix.

examples.label: Test results reference
examples.instruction: Find the skipped test.

title: Stack trace
summary: Show an error and where it happened without burying the useful line.
implemented: The error name and message, then your own frames; library and runtime frames fold behind a count that opens them. Paths wrap on narrow screens.
deferred: Frames are passed parsed; no parser for raw stack strings or source maps, and no open-in-editor links.

examples.label: Coding agent
examples.instruction: Open 3 library frames under the failing test.

examples.label: Stack trace reference
examples.instruction: Open the library frames.

title: Coding agent session
summary: Follow an agent's work on code: what it ran, read, changed and committed.
implemented: A reference specimen replaying a recorded session in which an agent fixes a failing test. The transcript shows reasoning, then tool calls whose results render richly: test results with a stack trace and the terminal output, the file read, the diff and the commit. Files beside it mark what the agent changed and preview each file as it stands at that point. The page opens complete; Replay plays it back and Show all skips to the end.
deferred: A recording, not a live agent: Tandem's own assistant works on projects, not code.

examples.label: Coding agent specimen
examples.instruction: Choose Replay, then open format-due.ts in Files after the edit.

title: Working plan
summary: Show what the assistant is doing for this request, step by step, while it works.
implemented: Multi-step replies (at-risk projects, this week, status updates, launch checklists) stream a working plan as a data part, replaced in place as each stage finishes: one task in progress, then done; a failed reply marks the current task blocked and a stopped one shows it as stopped. The plan docks above the composer as a collapsed bar with its title and progress that opens upward into the tasks.
deferred: The plan is scripted with each reply; a real agent would write and revise it as a tool call.

examples.label: Assistant
examples.instruction: Ask Draft a status update for Mobile app and open the bar above the composer while it works.

title: Conversation panel
summary: See everything a conversation did, made and cited, and get back to it.
implemented: A panel beside the chat (a sheet on narrower screens), opened from Conversation in the top bar or from a finished reply's reasoning. Work lists each question with a timeline of reasoning, steps, tool calls and answers, by state; Outputs lists drafted documents (Draft or Posted, with copy, download and the project) and tasks added, waiting or declined; Sources lists the cited pages once each. Items scroll the transcript to their reply and mark it for a moment.
deferred: The panel describes the open conversation only; history across conversations stays in the history list.

examples.label: Assistant
examples.instruction: Ask Which projects are at risk?, then select Thought for 1 second.

title: Agent runs
summary: Hand routine work on a record to an agent that runs in the background and asks before it changes anything.
implemented: A project's Agent tab starts a status report or a launch plan. The run reads the project step by step (each step says what it found and how long it took), keeps going if the person leaves, and stops at a review step: the report is edited and posted to Comments, or the proposed tasks are added, only on approval; Discard or Stop run end it with nothing changed. A failed step offers Try again or a way to continue without it (?scenario=run-failure). The tab is marked while a run needs the person, and earlier runs stay available from a run picker.
deferred: Runs are scripted from the project's records and timed in the browser; they are not scheduled, and there is no notification outside the project page.

examples.label: Project page
examples.instruction: Start Write a status report, then review and post the report.

examples.label: Failure
examples.instruction: Start Plan the launch; the second step fails once.

title: Area time series
summary: Compare how two flows move over time, such as work arriving and work getting done.
implemented: Analytics › Delivery: tasks completed and added as two gradient areas (shadcn's area chart), by day up to a month and by week beyond. The legend is a ChartSeriesToggle that shows and hides each series and keeps one on; with comparison, last period's completions follow as a keyed dashed line. Show data lists every point.
deferred: Stacked and 100% (expand) variants arrive with Workload (charts plan step 3); API key usage (step area) with step 4.

examples.label: Delivery
examples.instruction: Hide Added in the legend, then switch to Last 90 days to read by week.

title: Line with labelled points
summary: Show a trend whose values matter, readable without hovering.
implemented: Analytics › Delivery: median cycle time (days from adding a task to completing it) by week, as a line with its values on the points (shadcn's line chart with labels); daily medians are too noisy, so it reads by week past two weeks. The heading gives the period's median and, when comparing, whether it is faster or slower.
deferred: Burn-up with a due-date line and projection arrives with Projects (charts plan step 3).

examples.label: Cycle time
examples.instruction: Read the weekly medians on the points; choose Show data for the table.

title: Diverging bars
summary: Show change in both directions from zero, such as a backlog growing or shrinking.
implemented: Analytics › Delivery: tasks added minus tasks completed per day or week, above zero when the backlog grew and below when it shrank (shadcn's negative bar chart), in two poles no other Delivery series uses, with a Grew/Shrank key and a signed heading.

examples.label: Change in open tasks
examples.instruction: Weeks above the line added more work than they finished.

title: Chart states
summary: Say what a chart can't show: still loading, nothing in the range, or failed.
implemented: Kit ChartState: loading draws placeholder bars at the chart's size (the Overview chart's lazy fallback), empty says No data for this range with a way forward (Analytics charts for a quiet project or range, which also disable Show data), and failed offers Try again. Charts and their Show data tables keep the card's height.
deferred: A scripted failure scenario for charts is not offered; the failed state is shown in the reference.

examples.label: Empty range
examples.instruction: Launch campaign had no work in these days.
